accords.name: Citrus
accords.say: Peel oils: the brightest, quickest notes, gone first.

notes.name: Bergamot
notes.old: A small, bitter orange grown mostly in Calabria. Its peel oil is bright, floral and a little peppery, and it opens more perfumes than any other note.

notes.name: Bitter Orange
notes.old: The Seville orange. Its peel is darker and drier than sweet orange, and the same tree gives neroli and orange blossom.

notes.name: Blood Orange
notes.old: A red-fleshed orange: orange with a berry-like, slightly jammy tartness.

notes.name: Citron
notes.old: The ancient, knobbly ancestor of the lemon, pressed from its thick peel: dry and zesty, less sweet than lemon.

notes.name: Citrus
notes.old: No one fruit named: a mix of peel oils for a bright, sparkling opening.

notes.name: Clementine
notes.old: A small, sweet mandarin cross: soft, juicy and hardly bitter at all.

notes.name: Grapefruit
notes.old: Tart and faintly bitter-sulphurous; its key molecule (nootkatone) also smells a little of fresh wood.

notes.name: Green Mandarin
notes.old: Mandarin picked before it ripens: sharper and leafier than the sweet, candied ripe fruit.

notes.name: Lemon
notes.old: Cold-pressed from the peel: sharp, clean and quick to leave.

notes.name: Lime
notes.old: Greener and more bitter than lemon, with a sherbet fizz. Pressed, it is fresh; distilled, it turns candied.

notes.name: Orange
notes.old: Sweet orange peel: juicy, round and cheerful rather than sharp.

notes.name: Petitgrain
notes.old: Distilled from the leaves and green twigs of the bitter orange tree rather than its fruit: citrus gone green and woody, with a faint bitterness.

notes.name: Tangerine
notes.old: Close to mandarin: sweet and juicy, with a little tartness.

notes.name: Yuzu
notes.old: A Japanese citrus that smells like grapefruit, mandarin and lime at once, with a floral lift.

accords.name: Aromatic & Herbal
accords.say: Kitchen and hillside herbs: clean, camphorous, bitter-green.

notes.name: Artemisia
notes.old: A family of bitter, silvery herbs: dry, green and camphorous, with a medicinal edge.

notes.name: Basil
notes.old: Sweet, green and touched with anise, like the fresh leaves.

notes.name: Chamomile
notes.old: Apple-like, herbal and hay-sweet, like the tea.

notes.name: Clary Sage
notes.old: A sage that smells musky, tea-like and a little boozy, softer and warmer than kitchen sage.

notes.name: Davana
notes.old: An Indian artemisia that smells fruity, boozy and apricot-like. As an attar it is distilled into a base oil, often sandalwood.

notes.name: Eucalyptus
notes.old: Camphorous and cooling, like a chest rub; blue gum is the classic medicinal species.

notes.name: Herbal Notes
notes.old: A general herbal accord: dry, green, a little bitter, with no one herb named.

notes.name: Hops
notes.old: The flowers that make beer bitter: green, resinous and a little cheesy.

notes.name: Juniper Berry
notes.old: The berry-like cones that flavour gin: resinous, peppery and piney.

notes.name: Lavender
notes.old: Herbal, clean and slightly camphorous with a floral sweetness; the heart of the fougère. Lavender from Provence is the finer, sweeter kind.

notes.name: Lemon Verbena
notes.old: Intensely lemony leaves with a green, herbal sweetness: citrus without the fruit.

notes.name: Marjoram
notes.old: Soft, warm and herbal; gentler and sweeter than oregano.

notes.name: Mint
notes.old: Cool and sharp. Peppermint is the cold, menthol one and spearmint the sweeter, softer one; both touch the nerve that feels cold, so mint is felt as much as smelled.

notes.name: Myrtle
notes.old: A Mediterranean shrub: fresh and camphorous, somewhere between eucalyptus and bay.

notes.name: Oregano
notes.old: Pungent, dry and savoury: the pizza herb.

notes.name: Rosemary
notes.old: Sharp, camphorous and woody-green, like a sprig crushed between the fingers.

notes.name: Sage
notes.old: Common sage (salvia): dry, herbal and a little camphorous.

notes.name: Thyme
notes.old: Warm, dry and slightly medicinal, with a spicy herbal bite.

notes.name: Wormwood
notes.old: The artemisia that flavours absinthe: intensely bitter, green and faintly minty.

notes.name: Yarrow
notes.old: A field herb with a bitter, camphorous green smell and a hint of spice.

accords.name: Green
accords.say: Leaves, stems, grass and hay: the smell of plants rather than flowers.

notes.name: Crushed Leaves
notes.old: Leaves torn or crushed: a sharp, sappy green.

notes.name: Fig Leaf
notes.old: The leaves of the fig tree rather than its fruit: green, milky and faintly coconut.

notes.name: Galbanum
notes.old: A resin from a Persian plant related to fennel: piercingly green, bitter and earthy, like snapping a thick stem. A little goes a very long way.

notes.name: Grass
notes.old: Freshly cut or wild grass: sappy, green and sunny.

notes.name: Green Notes
notes.old: The general smell of cut leaves and stems, with no one plant named.

notes.name: Green Wheat
notes.old: Unripe wheat in the field: grassy, green and a little milky.

notes.name: Hay
notes.old: Dried grass, sweet and warm. The sweetness is coumarin, the same molecule as in tonka.

notes.name: Ivy
notes.old: A dark, bitter green, earthier and less sappy than grass.

notes.name: Poplar Bud
notes.old: The sticky spring buds of the poplar: resinous, honeyed and green, sold as balm of Gilead.

notes.name: Raspberry Leaf
notes.old: The soft, hay-like, tea-green leaves of the raspberry cane.

notes.name: Rhubarb
notes.old: Tart, sappy and green, with a pink sharpness.

notes.name: Sugar Cane
notes.old: Grassy, green and sweet, like chewing the raw cane.

notes.name: Sweet Vernalgrass
notes.old: A meadow grass whose coumarin gives fresh-cut hay its sweetness.

notes.name: Sweetgrass
notes.old: A prairie grass that smells of vanilla and hay, from coumarin. As bison grass it flavours Polish vodka.

notes.name: Tomato Leaf
notes.old: The sharp, pungent green that tomato plants leave on your fingers.

notes.name: Violet Leaf
notes.old: Cucumber-green and metallic-watery, nothing like the violet flower.

notes.name: Watercress
notes.old: Peppery, wet and green, like the salad leaf.

accords.name: Floral
accords.say: Petals and blossoms, real and reconstructed.

notes.name: Alpine Sandwort
notes.old: A small white flower of mountain scree. It names a clean, cool, high-meadow impression rather than an oil.

notes.name: Azure Bluet
notes.old: A tiny pale-blue wildflower. Here it stands for something delicate and airy rather than an extract.

notes.name: Bluebell
notes.old: Green, dewy woodland flowers, close to hyacinth.

notes.name: Carnation
notes.old: Spicy and floral, with a clove note running through it.

notes.name: Champaca
notes.old: A relative of magnolia from India: rich, tea-like, with an apricot note.

notes.name: Chrysanthemum
notes.old: Bitter-green, herbal and earthy: more leaf than petal.

notes.name: Clear Orchid
notes.old: An orchid made transparent: an airy floral note rather than a flower oil.

notes.name: Freesia
notes.old: Light, peppery and fresh, with a fruity edge.

notes.name: Gardenia
notes.old: A creamy white flower with a green, mushroomy edge. It gives almost no oil, so it is nearly always rebuilt from other materials.

notes.name: Geranium
notes.old: Rosy, green and a little minty. The leaves give a rose smell at a fraction of rose's price.

notes.name: Goldenrod
notes.old: Yellow late-summer flowers: herbal, honeyed and faintly medicinal.

notes.name: Green Tea Flowers
notes.old: The blossom of the tea bush: soft, green and faintly honeyed.

notes.name: Heliotrope
notes.old: Powdery and sweet, smelling of almond, vanilla and cherry pie.

notes.name: Honeysuckle
notes.old: Nectar-sweet, green and honeyed.

notes.name: Jasmine
notes.old: Heady, sweet and a little animalic (from indole, which also occurs in bodies). Sambac is the Arabian jasmine, greener and fruitier: the jasmine of jasmine tea.

notes.name: Lily
notes.old: Big lilies: spicy-sweet, with a green stem.

notes.name: Lily of the Valley
notes.old: Fresh, green, dewy bell-flowers. Nothing can be extracted from them, so the note is always built from molecules.

notes.name: Magnolia
notes.old: Creamy and lemony, a cool, fresh floral.

notes.name: Marigold
notes.old: The essential oil of tagetes (Mexican marigold): pungent, fruity-green and a little apple-like.

notes.name: Mimosa
notes.old: Soft yellow blossoms: powdery, with almond and honey.

notes.name: Mountain Wildflowers
notes.old: An impression of a high meadow in bloom: light, grassy and floral.

notes.name: Nectar
notes.old: The sweet liquid inside a flower: honeyed floral sweetness.

notes.name: Neroli
notes.old: Distilled from the same flowers as orange blossom: fresher, greener and more citrusy.

notes.name: Orange Blossom
notes.old: The flower of the bitter orange, extracted: honeyed, sweet and heady, richer than neroli.

notes.name: Orris
notes.old: What perfume calls iris comes from the root, aged for years before it is extracted: powdery, cool, earthy and buttery, with a violet edge. Orris butter is among the costliest materials in perfumery.

notes.name: Osmanthus
notes.old: A tiny Chinese flower that smells of apricot, leather and tea.

notes.name: Passionflower
notes.old: The flower of the passion-fruit vine: light and green-floral, usually built as an accord.

notes.name: Plum Blossom
notes.old: Delicate, almondy and faintly fruity.

notes.name: Pollen
notes.old: Dusty, honeyed and a little powdery.

notes.name: Rose
notes.old: The queen of florals: honeyed, fruity and a little spicy. Rose de Mai from Grasse is honeyed and fresh; Damask rose from Bulgaria or Turkey is rich and fruity; Taif rose from Saudi Arabia is spicy and intense. An absolute is extracted with solvents and is richer than the distilled oil.

notes.name: Snowdrops
notes.old: Delicate early-spring flowers: green, honeyed and cold.

notes.name: Tiare Flower
notes.old: The Tahitian gardenia, steeped in coconut oil for monoï: creamy and tropical.

notes.name: Tobacco Flower
notes.old: The flower of the tobacco plant, which opens at night: sweet, heavy and white-floral, not smoky.

notes.name: Tuberose
notes.old: A creamy, buttery, narcotic white flower, almost rubbery up close.

notes.name: Violet
notes.old: Sweet, powdery and candy-like, from ionones, the same molecules found in orris.

notes.name: Waterlily
notes.old: A watery, lightly fresh floral.

notes.name: White Lotus
notes.old: Aquatic, soft and powdery-sweet.

notes.name: Yellow Flowers
notes.old: A general sunny floral: honeyed and bright, with no one flower named.

notes.name: Ylang Ylang
notes.old: A tropical yellow flower: creamy, sweet like banana, with a little spice.

notes.name: Apple
notes.old: Crisp, juicy apple: green apple is sharp and tart, red apple sweeter and rounder. Apples give no oil, so it is always rebuilt from other materials.

notes.name: Apricot
notes.old: Soft, velvety stone fruit close to peach, jammy when preserved.

notes.name: Banana
notes.old: Sweet and creamy, with a slightly green, pear-drop edge.

notes.name: Blackberry
notes.old: A dark, tart berry, jammy when cooked.

notes.name: Blueberry
notes.old: Soft, sweet-tart and a little powdery.

notes.name: Cassis
notes.old: Blackcurrant: fruity and tart, with a pungent green edge from the buds.

notes.name: Cherry
notes.old: Red, sweet and almondy (the almond is benzaldehyde, which cherries share). Black cherry is darker and deeper.

notes.name: Cranberry
notes.old: Tart, bright and red.

notes.name: Dates
notes.old: Sticky, caramel-sweet dried fruit.

notes.name: Dried Fruits
notes.old: The concentrated, jammy sweetness of dried fruit: raisin, fig, prune.

notes.name: Fig
notes.old: The fruit: soft, milky and jammy-sweet.

notes.name: Goldenberry
notes.old: The Cape gooseberry: tart and tropical, a little like a sweet tomato.

notes.name: Green Apple
notes.old: Sharper and more tart than red apple, with a green snap.

notes.name: Guava
notes.old: Tropical and sweet, with a musky, green edge.

notes.name: Japanese Plum
notes.old: The loquat: sweet, apricot- and plum-like, with a floral edge.

notes.name: Litchi
notes.old: Lychee: rosy, juicy and sweet.

notes.name: Mango
notes.old: Juicy and tropical, a little resinous. Green mango is sharper and more resinous still.

notes.name: Maninka
notes.old: The fruit of a West African savannah tree: rendered in perfume as a juicy, nectar-sweet tropical fruit.

notes.name: Passionfruit
notes.old: Maracuja: sharp, sweet-sour and tropical.

notes.name: Peach
notes.old: Soft, velvety and sweet, with a creamy skin note.

notes.name: Pear
notes.old: Juicy, watery and sweet.

notes.name: Plum
notes.old: Dark, juicy and sweet-tart, with a slightly almond stone.

notes.name: Quince
notes.old: A hard, fragrant fruit between apple and pear, with a floral, honeyed perfume.

notes.name: Raspberry
notes.old: Bright and tart, with a violet-like sweetness.

notes.name: Red Berries
notes.old: A general accord of red berries: tart, bright and sweet.

notes.name: Scorched Pineapple
notes.old: Pineapple charred until it caramelises: smoky, sweet and tropical.

notes.name: Strawberry
notes.old: Sweet, jammy and red.

accords.name: Spice
accords.say: Seeds, barks, roots and peppers: heat, warmth and bite.

notes.name: Allspice
notes.old: One dried berry that smells like clove, cinnamon and nutmeg together.

notes.name: Anise
notes.old: Sweet licorice, as in aniseed and pastis.

notes.name: Black Pepper
notes.old: Dry, peppery heat with a fresh, woody lift.

notes.name: Caraway
notes.old: The rye-bread seed: warm and earthy, with a hint of anise.

notes.name: Cardamom
notes.old: Fresh, citrusy and camphorous, with a warm spice underneath.

notes.name: Cassia
notes.old: The bark of Chinese cinnamon: hotter, rougher and sweeter than true cinnamon. (Not cassie, the acacia flower.)

notes.name: Chilli
notes.old: Hot chilli: more idea than smell, since heat is felt rather than smelled. The Carolina Reaper is among the hottest chillies grown.

notes.name: Cinnamon
notes.old: Warm, sweet bark spice. Ceylon cinnamon is the lighter, more delicate kind.

notes.name: Clove
notes.old: Hot, sweet and almost medicinal, like the dentist's office or mulled wine.

notes.name: Coriander
notes.old: The seed: warm, spicy and a little citrusy and floral.

notes.name: Cumin
notes.old: Warm and earthy, with a sweaty, animal side that is hard to miss.

notes.name: Fenugreek
notes.old: Smells of maple syrup and curry at once.

notes.name: Ginger
notes.old: Fresh, zesty and warm-spicy. Fresh root is lemony; icy ginger leans cool and sparkling.

notes.name: Nutmeg
notes.old: Warm, sweet and woody, with a slightly soapy edge.

notes.name: Pink Pepper
notes.old: Baie rose: not a true pepper but a berry. Rosy, fresh and lightly peppery.

notes.name: Saffron
notes.old: The dried threads of a crocus: leathery, metallic, honeyed and warm.

notes.name: Spices
notes.old: A general warm spice accord, with no one spice named.

notes.name: Turmeric
notes.old: Earthy, warm and a little woody-bitter.

notes.name: Wasabi
notes.old: Sharp, nose-clearing heat with a green edge.

notes.name: Water Pepper
notes.old: A wetland plant (smartweed) with a peppery, green bite.

accords.name: Gourmand
accords.say: Things you could eat: sweets, grains, nuts, pastry.

notes.name: Almond
notes.old: Sweet and marzipan-like, from benzaldehyde. Burnt almond is toasted and nutty.

notes.name: Baked Apple
notes.old: Apple cooked soft with sugar and spice; a tarte tatin accord caramelises it.

notes.name: Balsamic Vinegar
notes.old: Sweet-sour and dark, like reduced grape must.

notes.name: Barley
notes.old: Toasty, nutty grain.

notes.name: Beeswax
notes.old: Honeyed, waxy and a little animalic, like an old candle.

notes.name: Black Walnut
notes.old: Walnut hull and wood: bitter, green and a little woody.

notes.name: Bread
notes.old: Warm, yeasty crust and crumb.

notes.name: Brown Sugar
notes.old: Molasses-rich sugar: deep and warm.

notes.name: Butter
notes.old: Rich, creamy and a little salty-sweet.

notes.name: Butterscotch
notes.old: Brown sugar cooked with butter: rich and caramel-sweet.

notes.name: Cacao
notes.old: The bean before it is chocolate: dry, bitter, earthy and powdery.

notes.name: Caramel
notes.old: Burnt sugar: sweet, rich and slightly bitter.

notes.name: Carob Pods
notes.old: The pods of the carob tree: sweet and earthy, like a dry, fruity cocoa.

notes.name: Chantilly Cream
notes.old: Sweetened whipped cream, often with vanilla.

notes.name: Chocolate
notes.old: Cocoa made into chocolate: bitter-sweet, creamy and rich. White chocolate is the cocoa butter with milk and sugar and no cocoa solids.

notes.name: Chocolate Cake
notes.old: Amandină is the Romanian one: a chocolate sponge soaked in chocolate syrup, layered with chocolate buttercream and glazed. Dark, sweet, moist and a little boozy.

notes.name: Cocoa Butter
notes.old: The fat of the cacao bean: soft, creamy and faintly chocolatey.

notes.name: Cocoa Pod
notes.old: The cocoa fruit itself, before its beans are fermented and roasted: a pale, tart-sweet, fruity pulp with the bitterness of cocoa underneath.

notes.name: Condensed Milk
notes.old: Cooked, sweetened milk: thick and caramel-sweet.

notes.name: Coumarin
notes.old: The molecule behind tonka and hay: sweet, almondy and warm. One of the first synthetics in modern perfumery.

notes.name: Edamame
notes.old: Young green soybeans still in the pod, steamed: beany, green, a little sweet and nutty.

notes.name: Halva
notes.old: The sesame sweet: nutty, sweet and a little dusty.

notes.name: Hazelnut
notes.old: Toasted and buttery, as in praline.

notes.name: Holy Bread
notes.old: Ataraxia's sacramental bread: the plain, warm smell of bread, lifted into something ritual.

notes.name: Honey
notes.old: Sweet, waxy and floral, with an animal edge in larger amounts. Black honey is darker and more bitter.

notes.name: Honeycomb
notes.old: Honey with the wax still in it: waxy, sweet and warm.

notes.name: Icing
notes.old: Powdered sugar: dry, sweet and powdery.

notes.name: Malt
notes.old: Sprouted, roasted grain: sweet, bready and a little like beer.

notes.name: Maple
notes.old: Maple syrup: sweet, woody and caramel.

notes.name: Milk
notes.old: Soft, creamy and lactonic, sometimes a little sour.

notes.name: Molasses
notes.old: The dark syrup left when sugar is refined: bitter-sweet and smoky.

notes.name: Murumuru Butter
notes.old: The fat of an Amazonian palm seed: soft, waxy and faintly nutty.

notes.name: Oat
notes.old: Soft, milky and cereal-sweet, like porridge.

notes.name: Pistachio
notes.old: Soft, green and nutty-sweet, a little milky.

notes.name: Potato
notes.old: Earthy, starchy and plain.

notes.name: Raisin Cookies
notes.old: Baked biscuit sweetness with dried fruit in it.

notes.name: Rice
notes.old: Steamed rice: soft, milky and a little powdery.

notes.name: Seed Cake
notes.old: A caraway-seeded cake (the one Bilbo offers his dwarves): buttery, warm and a little spicy.

notes.name: Sugar
notes.old: Plain sweetness, sometimes a little burnt.

notes.name: Tobacco
notes.old: Cured tobacco leaf: sweet, honeyed, hay-like and warm, not smoke. Blond tobacco is lighter and more honeyed; an absolute is the richest extract.

notes.name: Toffee
notes.old: Chewy, dark caramel.

notes.name: Tonka
notes.old: The seed of a South American tree. Coumarin gives it a smell of hay, almond, vanilla and tobacco.

notes.name: Vanilla
notes.old: The cured pod of an orchid: sweet, creamy and warm. Bourbon (from Madagascar) is the classic kind; an absolute is the richest extract.

notes.name: Wheat
notes.old: Dry grain and bread flour: warm, hay-like and cereal-sweet.

accords.name: Brews & Spirits
accords.say: Teas, coffee and what is poured from a bottle.

notes.name: Absinthe
notes.old: The anise-and-wormwood spirit: green, herbal and licorice-sweet.

notes.name: Amaretto
notes.old: The almond liqueur: sweet, marzipan and boozy.

notes.name: Coffee
notes.old: Roasted beans: bitter, toasty and warm. Coffee CO2 is extracted with carbon dioxide and smells closer to the fresh bean.

notes.name: Cognac
notes.old: Aged grape brandy: fruity, woody and warm from the cask.

notes.name: Cola
notes.old: The soft drink: sweet, citrusy and spiced, with vanilla and cinnamon.

notes.name: Green Tea
notes.old: Unoxidised tea: grassy, fresh and faintly bitter.

notes.name: Herbal Tea
notes.old: An infusion of herbs: soft, green and warm.

notes.name: Jasmine Tea
notes.old: Green tea scented with jasmine sambac blossoms.

notes.name: Lapsang Souchong
notes.old: Chinese black tea dried over pine fires: smoky, like a campfire in a cup.

notes.name: Liquor
notes.old: A general boozy note, with no one spirit named.

notes.name: Masala Chai
notes.old: Black tea brewed with milk and spices: cardamom, ginger, cinnamon, clove.

notes.name: Maté
notes.old: The South American herbal brew: grassy, smoky and a little like hay.

notes.name: Moroccan Tea
notes.old: Green tea steeped with fresh mint and sugar, as it is poured in Morocco.

notes.name: Oolong Tea
notes.old: Half-oxidised tea: floral, toasty and a little fruity.

notes.name: Root Beer
notes.old: Not beer: a sweet soft drink flavoured with sassafras or sarsaparilla root, wintergreen and vanilla. Minty, medicinal and creamy at once.

notes.name: Rum
notes.old: Sugar-cane spirit: sweet, boozy and molasses-dark. Rhum agricole is distilled from fresh cane juice and smells grassier.

notes.name: Soda Bubbles
notes.old: The fizz of soda: sparkling, sweet and light.

notes.name: Sparkling Water
notes.old: Carbonated water: a cold, fizzing freshness rather than a smell.

notes.name: Tea
notes.old: Dried tea leaves: dry, astringent and a little smoky-sweet. Black tea is the fully oxidised kind.

notes.name: Amber Oud
notes.old: Oud set in a warm, sweet amber accord.

notes.name: Amberwood
notes.old: Modern woody-amber molecules: dry, warm, diffusive and sometimes sharp.

notes.name: Amyris
notes.old: West Indian 'sandalwood', though unrelated: soft, woody and a little balsamic.

notes.name: Bark
notes.old: Tree bark: dry, woody and a little bitter.

notes.name: Birch
notes.old: Birch wood and bark: clean, green and lightly smoky.

notes.name: Cashmeran
notes.old: A synthetic molecule: soft, musky and woody, like warm cashmere.

notes.name: Cedarwood
notes.old: Dry, pencil-shaving wood. Atlas cedar is sweeter and more balsamic; Virginia cedar is the pencil. A tincture is wood steeped in alcohol.

notes.name: Cypriol
notes.old: Nagarmotha: the root of a sedge. Smoky, woody and leathery, close to vetiver and oud.

notes.name: Edelwood Oil
notes.old: A wood oil Pineward names in Gristmill, beside cedar planks, sawdust and smouldering logs; the house does not say what tree it comes from.

notes.name: Guaiac Wood
notes.old: A South American wood: smoky, sweet and a little like tar and roses.

notes.name: Mahogany
notes.old: A dense, dark red wood: dry and faintly spicy.

notes.name: Moldy Cedarwood
notes.old: Cedar gone damp and mouldy: Tombstone's Sweet Coffin, the wood of a coffin in wet ground.

notes.name: Oak
notes.old: Dry, tannic wood, like the inside of a barrel.

notes.name: Oud
notes.old: Agarwood: the dark, resin-soaked heartwood of the aquilaria tree, formed when it is infected by a mould. Deep, woody, leathery and animalic, and each region's oud smells different: Cambodian sweet and fruity, Indian (Assam) barnyard-heavy, Malaysian and Thai in between.

notes.name: Patchouli
notes.old: The leaves of an Asian mint relative: earthy, damp, dark and a little chocolatey. Aceh, in Indonesia, gives a prized dark kind.

notes.name: Petrified Driftwood
notes.old: Wood that the sea has worn and time turned to stone: salty, dry and mineral.

notes.name: Pineboard
notes.old: A sawn pine plank: resinous and sweet-woody.

notes.name: Sandalwood
notes.old: Creamy, milky and softly woody. Mysore sandalwood from India is the legendary, now very rare kind; Australian sandalwood is lighter and greener.

notes.name: Sawdust
notes.old: Freshly cut wood: dry, sweet and dusty.

notes.name: Teak Wood
notes.old: A dense, oily tropical wood: dry, leathery and warm.

notes.name: Vetiver
notes.old: The root of a tropical grass: earthy, smoky, woody and a little nutty. Haitian vetiver is the cleaner kind; Bourbon vetiver, from Réunion, the smokier.

notes.name: Willow Bark
notes.old: Bitter, green and faintly medicinal: the bark aspirin was first found in.

notes.name: Woody Notes
notes.old: A general dry wood accord, with no one tree named.

accords.name: Conifers
accords.say: Needles, cones and the trees that carry them.

notes.name: Black Hemlock
notes.old: A mountain hemlock: soft, resinous needles.

notes.name: Cedar Leaf
notes.old: Thuja: the leaves of the western red cedar. Sharp, green and camphorous.

notes.name: Cypress
notes.old: Dry, green and woody, with a smoky, resinous edge.

notes.name: Fir
notes.old: Soft, sweet and balsamic: the Christmas-tree smell. Balsam fir is the sweetest; silver and noble firs are fresher. Momi is the Japanese fir.

notes.name: Juniper
notes.old: The shrubby conifer itself: sharp, dry needles with a gin-like tang.

notes.name: Larch Cones
notes.old: Small, woody cones: resinous and dry.

notes.name: Nootka
notes.old: The Nootka cypress, or Alaska yellow cedar: dry, clean and woody, with a grapefruit note.

notes.name: Pine
notes.old: Resinous, sharp and fresh, like a forest after rain. Scotch pine is the classic; mugo is the low mountain pine.

notes.name: Pine Needles
notes.old: The needles themselves: green, sharp and fresh. Dried or frozen, they are drier or colder; ponderosa needles have a vanilla-butterscotch edge.

notes.name: Snoqualmie Forest Evergreens
notes.old: Pineward's name for the conifers of Washington State's Snoqualmie forest: damp, green and resinous.

notes.name: Spruce
notes.old: Sharp, green and a little citrusy: the smell of spruce tips.

notes.name: Tamarack
notes.old: The American larch: soft, sweet and resinous.

accords.name: Resins & Balsams
accords.say: What trees weep: incense, amber and balm.

notes.name: Amber
notes.old: Not a material but an accord: labdanum, benzoin and vanilla, warm, sweet and resinous. It has nothing to do with the fossil. White amber is lighter and more musky; mineral ambers are drier.

notes.name: Balsam
notes.old: A general balsamic note: warm, sweet, resinous.

notes.name: Benzoin
notes.old: A resin that smells of vanilla, caramel and cinnamon. Siam benzoin, from Laos and Thailand, is the sweetest.

notes.name: Dragon's Blood
notes.old: A deep red resin: sweet, woody and a little powdery.

notes.name: Elemi
notes.old: A resin with a lemony, peppery, fresh smell, the lightest of the incenses.

notes.name: Frankincense
notes.old: Olibanum: the resin of a desert tree. Lemony, peppery and smoky, like a church.

notes.name: Incense
notes.old: The smoke of burning resins: frankincense, myrrh, church and temple.

notes.name: Labdanum
notes.old: A gum from the rockrose shrub, once combed from the beards of goats: dark, leathery, ambery and animalic. The heart of the amber accord.

notes.name: Myrrh
notes.old: A resin: bitter, medicinal, mushroomy and warm. Sweet myrrh is opoponax.

notes.name: Opoponax
notes.old: Sweet myrrh: warm, sweet, powdery-balsamic, softer than myrrh.

notes.name: Peru Balsam
notes.old: A balsam that smells of vanilla, cinnamon and warm resin.

notes.name: Ponderosa Resin
notes.old: The sap of the ponderosa pine: sweet and resinous, with a vanilla note.

notes.name: Propolis
notes.old: The resinous glue bees seal their hives with: balsamic, honeyed and medicinal.

notes.name: Resins
notes.old: A general resinous accord, warm and balmy, with no one resin named.

notes.name: Rum Resin
notes.old: A resinous note with a sweet, boozy, rum-like warmth.

notes.name: Sandarac
notes.old: A resin from a North African cypress, used in old varnishes: dry, resinous and a little fresh.

notes.name: Sawn Resin
notes.old: Resin freshly cut through with the wood: sharp, sappy and balsamic.

notes.name: Styrax
notes.old: A balsam: leathery, smoky and a little like cinnamon and plastic.

notes.name: Tolu Balsam
notes.old: A balsam, sweeter and lighter than Peru balsam: vanilla and toffee.

notes.name: Turpentine
notes.old: Distilled from pine resin: sharp, solvent-like and piney, the smell of an artist's studio.

accords.name: Musk, Skin & Animalic
accords.say: Musks, leathers and the warmth of bodies.

notes.name: Ambergris
notes.old: A waxy substance from the sperm whale, aged by the sea for years: salty, sweet, marine and skin-like. Nearly always synthetic now.

notes.name: Ambrette
notes.old: A hibiscus seed that smells musky, pear-like and winey: the plant-world's musk.

notes.name: Animal Notes
notes.old: A general animalic accord: warm, dirty and skin-like.

notes.name: Botanical Musk
notes.old: Musk from plants rather than molecules or animals, such as ambrette seed.

notes.name: Castoreum
notes.old: Once taken from the beaver, now reconstructed: leathery, smoky and animal.

notes.name: Civet
notes.old: Once from the civet cat, now synthetic: faecal on its own, warm and radiant in a trace.

notes.name: Costus
notes.old: A root whose oil smells like unwashed hair and animal fur: dirty, warm and waxy.

notes.name: Goat Hair
notes.old: The smell of goat: warm, sweaty and animal. A tincture is the hair steeped in alcohol, most famously in Haxan.

notes.name: Hyrax
notes.old: Africa stone: the fossilised droppings of the rock hyrax. Animalic, leathery and a little like tobacco.

notes.name: Lanolin
notes.old: The fat of sheep's wool: waxy, soft and faintly animal.

notes.name: Leather
notes.old: Tanned hide: smoky, birch-tarry, a little sweet.

notes.name: Musk
notes.old: Once taken from musk deer, now made from molecules: soft, clean, skin-like warmth. White musk is the laundered, cleanest kind; Tonkin musk names the old deer musk.

notes.name: Sheep Wool
notes.old: Warm wool: lanolin, animal and a little sweet.

notes.name: Skin
notes.old: The warm, slightly salty smell of skin, built from musks.

notes.name: Suede
notes.old: Soft, powdery leather: lighter and cleaner than leather.

notes.name: Cedarmoss
notes.old: Moss from Moroccan cedars: a gentler, woodier cousin of oakmoss.

notes.name: Concrete
notes.old: Cement and dust: dry, chalky and urban; wet, it smells of rain on a pavement.

notes.name: Damp Vegetation
notes.old: Wet leaves and undergrowth: green, rotting-sweet and earthy.

notes.name: Dust
notes.old: Dry, powdery and a little sweet, like a room nobody has opened.

notes.name: Lichen
notes.old: Crusty growths on rock and bark: dry, earthy and mineral.

notes.name: Mineral Accord
notes.old: Stone, chalk and flint: dry, cool and mineral.

notes.name: Moss
notes.old: Damp green moss on stone and bark.

notes.name: Mushroom
notes.old: Damp, earthy and umami. Morel is nutty and smoky; oyster mushroom is softer.

notes.name: Oakmoss
notes.old: A lichen that grows on oaks: damp, earthy, inky and green. The base of the chypre, now limited by safety rules.

notes.name: Peat
notes.old: Decayed moss: smoky, earthy and damp, as in Islay whisky.

notes.name: Petrichor
notes.old: The smell of rain on dry ground: geosmin and the oils stone holds.

notes.name: Sand
notes.old: Warm, dry and mineral; sun-burnt sand is hot and salty.

notes.name: Soil
notes.old: Earth: damp, rooty and dark, from geosmin, the molecule of wet earth. A tincture is earth steeped in alcohol.

notes.name: Spikenard
notes.old: Jatamansi, a Himalayan root: earthy, musty and woody, between valerian, patchouli and old leather.

notes.name: Swamp Water
notes.old: Still, dark water: green, muddy and a little rotten.

notes.name: Treemoss
notes.old: A lichen from pine and fir: darker, smokier and more resinous than oakmoss.

notes.name: Wet Stone
notes.old: Rain on rock: cold, mineral and clean.

accords.name: Water & Air
accords.say: Sea, rain, steam and open sky.

notes.name: Airy Note
notes.old: A light, diffusive note that gives air and space rather than a smell.

notes.name: Aquatic Notes
notes.old: Clean water, built from molecules such as Calone: fresh, cool and faintly melon-like.

notes.name: Clear Skies
notes.old: An impression of open, cloudless sky: airy, cool and clean.

notes.name: Cold Night Air
notes.old: An impression of cold air after dark: sharp, clean and empty.

notes.name: Dead Water
notes.old: Tombstone's water gone still and stale: the dark, unmoving water round a sunken coffin.

notes.name: Marine Accord
notes.old: The sea: salty, windy and fresh.

notes.name: Ozone
notes.old: The smell of air after a storm: sharp, clean and metallic.

notes.name: Rain Notes
notes.old: Falling rain: wet, cool and fresh.

notes.name: Sea Salt
notes.old: Dry salt crystals and spray: mineral, salty and skin-like.

notes.name: Sea Water
notes.old: Salt water: fresh, mineral and a little green.

notes.name: Seaweed
notes.old: Kelp and bladderwrack: salty, iodine-green and a little fishy. Irish sea moss is a red seaweed.

notes.name: Solar Notes
notes.old: The warmth of sun on skin and sand: salty, floral and a little like sunscreen.

notes.name: Steam
notes.old: Warm water vapour: soft, damp and clean.

accords.name: Smoke & Char
accords.say: Fire, tar and what burning leaves behind.

notes.name: Ash
notes.old: What is left after the fire: cold, dry and grey.

notes.name: Birch Tar
notes.old: Tar distilled from birch bark: smoky, leathery and medicinal; it tans Russian leather.

notes.name: Fire
notes.old: Open flame: hot, dry, crackling smoke.

notes.name: Gasoline
notes.old: Petrol: sharp, volatile and chemical.

notes.name: Palo Santo
notes.old: A South American wood burned like incense: citrusy, minty and resinous. Smoked, it becomes sweet smoke.

notes.name: Pine Tar
notes.old: Tar from pine wood: dark, smoky and resinous, the smell of old ships and baseball bats.

notes.name: Smoke
notes.old: Burning wood and leaves: dry, bitter and warm.

notes.name: Smouldering Logs
notes.old: Wood burning slowly without flame: soft, sweet smoke.

accords.name: Impressions
accords.say: Notes that are not materials: objects, places, feelings, named by a house.

notes.name: Aged Parchment
notes.old: Old animal-skin paper: dry, dusty, a little leathery.

notes.name: Blush
notes.old: The powdery smell of makeup blush.

notes.name: Candle Wax
notes.old: Paraffin and beeswax: warm, waxy and faintly smoky.

notes.name: CO2 Extracts
notes.old: Materials extracted with carbon dioxide under pressure instead of heat or solvents, so they smell closer to the raw plant. Named as a note, it says how, not what.

notes.name: Decayed Rose
notes.old: A rose past its best: jammy, earthy and a little rotten.

notes.name: Dried Blood
notes.old: Metallic and iron-rich: the smell of blood gone dry.

notes.name: Dusty Antiques
notes.old: An antique shop: old wood, dust, polish and metal.

notes.name: Dusty Sofa
notes.old: An old upholstered chair: dust, fabric and the people who sat in it.

notes.name: Eye Pencil
notes.old: The waxy, woody smell of a cosmetic pencil.

notes.name: Gold
notes.old: Ataraxia names it and does not say what it is made of: an impression of warmth and richness.

notes.name: Instant Film
notes.old: The chemical smell of a freshly developing Polaroid.

notes.name: Lip Gloss
notes.old: Sweet, fruity and waxy.

notes.name: Lipstick
notes.old: Waxy, powdery and floral, like the inside of a lipstick tube: violet and rose.

notes.name: Makeup Palette
notes.old: Pressed powders and waxes: a vanity drawer.

notes.name: Mousse de Saxe
notes.old: A classic base from around 1900: geranium, licorice, vanilla and a smoky leather molecule. Sweet, powdery and animalic, the smell of old Carons.

notes.name: Old Books
notes.old: Library shelves: dust, paper, glue and leather, sweetened by decaying lignin.

notes.name: Oriental Notes
notes.old: The old name for the amber family: warm, sweet, spicy and resinous. The industry now calls it 'amber'.

notes.name: Paper
notes.old: Clean paper: dry, woody and faintly sweet.

notes.name: Porcelain
notes.old: Smooth, cool and clean: a feeling more than a smell.

notes.name: Rotten Flesh
notes.old: Decay, named as a note for its darkness rather than recreated in full.

notes.name: Salty Tears
notes.old: Salt and skin: a mineral, slightly bodily note.

notes.name: Spinal Fluid
notes.old: Ataraxia's conceptual note: clear, cold, clinical, bodily.

notes.name: Velvet
notes.old: Soft, powdery, rich texture made into smell.

notes.name: Westfarthing Leaf
notes.old: Pipe-weed from the Shire, after Tolkien: Pineward's tobacco, named for the Hobbits' best.
